newsitem.title: NIGERIA: Nigerian conglomerates depress share trading.
newsitem.headline: Nigerian conglomerates depress share trading.

text.p: Shares of Nigeria's leading conglomerates fell heavily in Wednesday's trade on persistent selling, dealers said.
The all-share index fell to 8434.55 from 8458.29 on Tuesday.
Dealers said it was the index's lowest level since the current bearish trend, which has pushed it down steadily from an all-time high of 8805 in late April.
Traders blame a gloomy economic outlook and slow business activities caused by the government's reluctance to release funds for infrastructure development for the trend.
"Most companies are groaning under the impact of these negative factors and profits look set to fall," one trader said.
Conglomerate PZ Industries PZIN.LG, the market's most capitalised firm, plunged by 70 kobo to close at 27.50 naira.
Lever Brothers and UAC fell five kobo each to close at 27.95 naira and 16.40 naira, respectively.
Coca-Cola bottler Nigerian Bottling Company lost 20 kobo to 54.00 naira as investors continued to dump the stock.
"The market currently feels that most of these companies are over-priced," one dealer said.
West African Portland Cement Company and Cadbury lost 10 kobo each to 62.00 naira and 35.80 naira, respectively.
Unipetrol was the biggest oil marketer to slide, ending 10 kobo weaker at 67.80 naira. Agip at 17.40 naira and Total at 58.15 naira, fell five kobo each.
Hospital group Ekocorp went ex-dividend at 4.75 naira, down 25 kobo.
The few gainers were led by construction firm Cappa and D'Alberto, which rose five kobo to 12.30 naira.
Oil miller P.S. Mandrides gained five kobo to 6.40 naira while Wema Bank climbed two kobo to 3.50 naira.
